title: Quiz goal step: ranges instead of a number field
author: Aminat Oyediran
surface: DTC assessment quiz, paid social traffic, mobile-first, UK
hypothesis: Because quiz starters drop off at the 'how much weight do you want to lose?' step when asked to type a precise number, replacing the open number field with four goal ranges will increase quiz completion rate, because it removes both the effort of choosing a number and the discomfort of disclosing one.

brief.problem: Session recordings (n=120, Sept 2026) show 38% of quiz starters abandon at the goal step, the highest single-step drop in the flow. 14 of the 31 abandoners who were later surveyed said they 'didn't know what number to put'. Support tickets mention the step 9 times in the last month. GA4 confirms median time on this step is 2.4x the next slowest step.
priorEvidence: June 2026: shortening the quiz from 11 to 8 steps lifted completion 6% (shipped). The goal step was kept.
No previous test on input type at this step.
brief.control: Current goal step: single open numeric field labelled 'How much weight do you want to lose? (kg)', Continue button disabled until a value is entered.

variants.name: Variant B
variants.change: Replace the numeric field with four tappable range cards: 'Under 5 kg', '5 to 10 kg', '10 to 20 kg', 'More than 20 kg'. Selecting a card advances automatically. Everything else on the step is unchanged.
variants.headline: What's your goal?
variants.supporting: Pick the range that feels right. You can change it later.
variants.rationale: Removes the precision demand and the disclosure anxiety of typing a number.

brief.audience: All new visitors who start the quiz from paid social landing pages, UK, any device.
brief.excluded: Returning visitors with an existing account, internal IPs, visitors arriving from email or retargeting, and anyone already in the pricing-page test.
brief.entryPoint: Assignment happens on quiz start (first step viewed), not on page load, so bounces before the quiz do not dilute the sample.
brief.unitOfRandomisation: User (first-party cookie ID, sticky across sessions). Session-level assignment would let one person see both versions across visits and contaminate the result.

primaryMetric.name: Quiz completion rate
primaryMetric.numerator: Users who reach the quiz results screen
primaryMetric.attributionWindow: Same session as assignment, plus 24 hours for returns via the resume link

secondaryMetrics: Drop-off rate at the goal step specifically
Median time on the goal step
guardrails: Checkout rate from quiz completers must not fall by more than 2% relative (the ranges must not attract less-qualified completers)
Revenue per quiz start must not fall
Quiz step load time stays under 1.5 s on mobile
brief.mdeRationale: An 8% relative lift on 22% completion is about 158 extra completions a week at current traffic, which at the current completer-to-checkout rate is worth roughly £9k a month in first orders. Anything smaller would not justify the design and engineering time plus the follow-on work on the other steps.
brief.successCriteria: At the pre-registered end of week 2, Variant B is a win if quiz completion is at least 23.76% (8% relative on the 22% baseline) with p < 0.05 two-sided and all three guardrails hold. It is a loss if completion is significantly lower, or if the checkout guardrail is breached regardless of the completion result. Anything else is inconclusive and the test is not extended.

decisionRules.win: Ship range cards to 100%, then test the same pattern on the 'current weight' step, which has the second-highest drop.
decisionRules.loss: Keep the number field. Next test reassurance copy under the field ('Just a rough idea is fine'), since the drop may be about disclosure rather than effort.
decisionRules.flat: Conclude input type is not the driver at this step and move to the next-highest drop step instead of iterating here.

brief.baselineSource: GA4, quiz starts to results screen, 1 Aug to 28 Sept 2026, same audience definition as the test.
brief.trafficAllocation: 50/50 from launch. No ramp: the change is low-risk and a ramp would push the end date out.
brief.stoppingRule: Run the full pre-registered 2 weeks and read once at the end. No interim significance reads. The only early stop is a guardrail breach of more than 10% relative on checkout rate confirmed over 3 consecutive days, or a tracking fault.
segmentsToWatch: iOS vs Android (the number keypad behaves differently)
New vs returning within the eligible population
risks: The pricing-page test runs concurrently; eligibility excludes its participants to avoid interaction.
A new paid social campaign launches in week 2 and may shift the audience mix; both arms are exposed equally but the pooled baseline may move.
Novelty effect is unlikely for a form input but completion will be re-read 4 weeks after shipping.
qaChecks: Assignment event fires once per user and matches the arm shown (checked on iOS Safari, Android Chrome, desktop Chrome)
Results-screen event fires for both arms and the goal value is stored in the same field for ranges and numbers
Sample ratio check at 48 hours: arms within 1% of 50/50 or the test is paused

owners.build: Front-end engineer on the growth squad (design from the product designer)
owners.analysis: Aminat Oyediran, with the data analyst reviewing the read-out
owners.decision: Head of Growth, on the pre-registered criteria above
